It is completely understandable to feel hurt or confused by this situation. In professional counseling, transitioning from individual to couples therapy with the same counselor is often discouraged because it creates an inherent imbalance. Furthermore, a key principle of couples counseling is that the relationship itself is the client. It is generally not considered acceptable or effective practice for a therapist to explicitly "take sides." A counselor's role is to facilitate healthy communication and understanding, not to act as a judge. 

When a therapist takes one partner aside and then declares they are siding with them, it breaks down the trust and safety essential for therapy. Because of these ethical complexities, it is usually recommended to use a separate, neutral couples counselor so both partners start on equal footing. You have every right to discuss how this made you feel with the counselor, or to seek a new therapist if the trust in this professional relationship has been broken.
